# i3dnet_flexmetal_server (Resource)

FlexMetal servers are physical servers that can be requested and released at will.

A How to Guide is available at this URL : https://docs.i3d.net/compute/flexmetal/api

~> **Note on import:** the API does not return `ssh_key`, `post_install_script`, `os.kernel_params`, `os.partitions` or `os.ipxe_script_url`, so an imported server has these unset. Add them to your configuration to match the server as it was provisioned; note that a change to `post_install_script` forces replacement.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Create a Flexmetal Server
resource "i3dnet_flexmetal_server" "my-server" {
  name          = "TerraFlex-Server"
  location      = "EU: Rotterdam"
  instance_type = "bm7.std.8"
  os = {
    slug = "ubuntu-2404-lts"
    kernel_params = [
      {
        key   = "KEY_A"
        value = "VALUE_A"
      }
    ]
  }
  ssh_key             = ["<YOUR-PUBLIC-SSH-KEY>"]
  post_install_script = "#!/bin/bash\necho \"Hi TerraFlex there!\" > /root/output.txt"
}

# Create a partitioned Flexmetal Server On-Demand
resource "i3dnet_flexmetal_server" "my-partitioned-server" {
  name          = "TerraFlex-Server"
  location      = "EU: Rotterdam"
  instance_type = "bm7.std.8"
  os = {
    slug = "ubuntu-2404-lts"
    kernel_params = [
      {
        key   = "KEY_A"
        value = "VALUE_A"
      }
    ]
    partitions = [
      {
        "target" : "/boot",
        "filesystem" : "ext2",
        "size" : 4096
      },
      {
        "target" : "/",
        "filesystem" : "ext4",
        "size" : -1
      },
      {
        "target"     = "/custom",
        "filesystem" = "ext4",
        "size"       = 10240
      }
    ]
  }
  ssh_key             = ["<YOUR-PUBLIC-SSH-KEY>"]
  post_install_script = "#!/bin/bash\necho \"Hi TerraFlex there!\" > /root/output.txt"
}

# Create a Talos OS 1.9.0 server On-Demand with custom timeout for create resource of 30 minutes. Default timeout is 45 minutes.
resource "i3dnet_flexmetal_server" "my-talos" {
  name          = "talosHostName"
  location      = "EU: Rotterdam"
  instance_type = "bm7.std.8"
  os = {
    slug = "talos-omni-190"
    kernel_params = [
      {
        key   = "siderolink.api"
        value = "https://siderolink.api/?jointoken=secret"
      },
      {
        key   = "talos.customparam"
        value = "123456"
      }
    ]
  }
  timeouts = {
    create = "30m" // duration is specified as Terraform string (e.g., "30m", "1h")
  }
}

# Create a Talos OS 1.9.0 server under committed capacity contract `CONTRACT-123`
resource "i3dnet_flexmetal_server" "my-talos" {
  name          = "MyTalosServer"
  location      = "EU: Rotterdam"
  instance_type = "bm7.std.8"
  os = {
    slug = "talos-omni-190"
    kernel_params = [
      {
        key   = "siderolink.api"
        value = "https://siderolink.api/?jointoken=secret"
      }
    ]
  }
  contract_id = "CONTRACT-123"
}

# Create a Talos OS 1.9.0 server under committed capacity contract `CONTRACT-123`
# You can add overflow = true to request server On-Demand if committed capacity is full
resource "i3dnet_flexmetal_server" "my-talos" {
  name          = "MyTalosServer"
  location      = "EU: Rotterdam"
  instance_type = "bm7.std.8"
  os = {
    slug = "talos-omni-190"
    kernel_params = [
      {
        key   = "siderolink.api"
        value = "https://siderolink.api/?jointoken=secret"
      }
    ]
  }
  contract_id = "CONTRACT-123"
  overflow    = true
}

# Create a Custom iPXE server
resource "i3dnet_flexmetal_server" "my-custom-ipxe" {
  name          = "MyCustomIpxeServer"
  location      = "EU: Rotterdam"
  instance_type = "bm7.std.8"
  os = {
    slug          = "custom-ipxe"
    ipxeScriptUrl = "https://example.org/custom-ipxe.cfg"
  }
}
# Attach a server to networks you created with the Dedicated Networks API (https://docs.i3d.net/connectivity/dedicated-networks-api).
# The networks and prefixes must already exist; refer to them with data sources. Changing `networks` replaces the server.
data "i3dnet_network" "prod" {
  id = "01928f3e-7c4a-7b1e-9d2f-3a5b6c7d8e9f"
}

data "i3dnet_network" "backend" {
  id = "01984f2e-1c3a-7d21-9d10-3542f27adccf"
}

data "i3dnet_network_prefixes" "prod_ipv4" {
  network_id = data.i3dnet_network.prod.id
  family     = 4
}

resource "i3dnet_flexmetal_server" "my-networked-server" {
  name          = "MyNetworkedServer"
  location      = "EU: Rotterdam"
  instance_type = "bm7.std.8"
  os = {
    slug = "ubuntu-2404-lts"
  }
  ssh_key = ["<YOUR-PUBLIC-SSH-KEY>"]
  networks = [
    {
      # Untagged, with an IPv6 address and an IPv4 address from a chosen prefix
      network_id = data.i3dnet_network.prod.id
      ip_allocations = [
        { family = 6 },
        { prefix_id = data.i3dnet_network_prefixes.prod_ipv4.prefixes[0].id },
      ]
    },
    {
      # A tagged 802.1Q VLAN without addresses (layer 2 only)
      network_id     = data.i3dnet_network.backend.id
      tagged         = true
      ip_allocations = []
    },
  ]
}

output "my_networked_server_ipv4" {
  value = i3dnet_flexmetal_server.my-networked-server.networks[0].ip_allocations[1].address
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `instance_type` (String) Server instance type. Available instance types can be obtained from [/v3/flexMetal/location/{locationId}}/instanceTypes](https://docs.i3d.net/api/api_general#get-v3-flexmetal-location-locationid-instancetypes). Use the `name` field from the response.
- `location` (String) Server location. Available locations can be obtained from [/v3/flexMetal/location](https://docs.i3d.net/api/api_general#get-v3-flexmetal-location). Use the `name` field from the response.
- `name` (String) Server name or hostname, depending on the chosen OS. E.g. Talos requires a hostname but regular Linux OSs work with either.
- `os` (Attributes) Server operating system. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--os))

### Optional

- `contract_id` (String) Represents client contractId. Format is ^[A-Z0-9_\-.]{0,240}$
- `networks` (Attributes List) The networks to attach the server to, in this order: untagged or as tagged (802.1Q) VLANs, with addresses from the prefixes you choose, or without addresses (`ip_allocations = []`). Leave it out for the default network and addresses. The networks and prefixes must already exist: create them with the [Dedicated Networks API](https://docs.i3d.net/connectivity/dedicated-networks-api) and refer to them with the `i3dnet_network`, `i3dnet_networks` and `i3dnet_network_prefixes` data sources. Changing `networks` replaces the server. A network created just before the apply can still be provisioning; the delivery waits for it, so raise `timeouts.create` in that case. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--networks))
- `overflow` (Boolean) If true, the server will be created even if the location is at commited capacity. Default is false.
- `post_install_script` (String) Post install script. A shell script (e.g. bash) that will be executed after your OS is installed. Currently only supported for Linux based operating systems.
- `ssh_key` (List of String) A list of SSH keys. You can either supply SSH key UUIDs from stored objects in [/v3/sshKey](https://docs.i3d.net/api/api_general#get-v3-sshkey) or provide public keys directly. SSH keys are installed for the root user.
- `tags` (List of String) A list of tags. There is a maximum of 60 tags per server. Each tag must adhere to this pattern: ^[A-Za-z0-9_:-]{1,64}$
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (Number) Server creation timestamp.
- `delivered_at` (Number) Server delivery timestamp.
- `ip_addresses` (Attributes List) Server IP address details. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--ip_addresses))
- `released_at` (Number) Server release timestamp.
- `status` (String) Server delivery status.<br /><li><ul>created</ul><ul>discovering</ul><ul>discovered</ul><ul>allocating</ul><ul>allocated</ul><ul>configuring_network</ul><ul>network_configured</ul><ul>provisioning</ul><ul>provisioned</ul><ul>delivered</ul><ul>failed</ul><ul>releasing</ul><ul>released</ul></li>
- `status_message` (String) Status message.
- `uuid` (String) Server UUID.

<a id="nestedatt--os"></a>
### Nested Schema for `os`

Required:

- `slug` (String) Identifier of the OS. Available operating systems can be obtained from [/v3/operatingsystem](https://docs.i3d.net/api/api_general#get-v3-operatingsystem). Use the `slug` field from the response.

Optional:

- `ipxe_script_url` (String) The URL to your custom iPXE boot menu file. Can and must be used in combination with OS slug custom-ipxe.
- `kernel_params` (Attributes List) Kernel params for the PXE stage of the OS installation. Most operating systems do not require these, but e.g. Talos does. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--os--kernel_params))
- `partitions` (Attributes List) Custom partitions for the OS installation. If not provided, the default partitioning scheme will be used. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--os--partitions))

<a id="nestedatt--os--kernel_params"></a>
### Nested Schema for `os.kernel_params`

Required:

- `key` (String) Key of the kernel param
- `value` (String) Value of the kernel param


<a id="nestedatt--os--partitions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `os.partitions`

Required:

- `filesystem` (String) Type of filesystem to use for the target. Allowed: ext2, ext3, ext4, xfs
- `size` (Number) The size of the partition, in MB. Use -1 to indicate usage of the remaining space on the disk.
- `target` (String) Mount point for the partition



<a id="nestedatt--networks"></a>
### Nested Schema for `networks`

Required:

- `network_id` (String) ID of a network you created with the Dedicated Networks API, in the same fabric as the server's location. Each network at most once.

Optional:

- `ip_allocations` (Attributes List) The addresses the server gets in this network, in this order. Leave it out for the default addresses; `[]` means layer 2 only. Each entry sets either `family` (4 or 6) or `prefix_id`; the other is filled in from the response. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--networks--ip_allocations))
- `tagged` (Boolean) false (default): the network is untagged on the server's interface; true: a tagged 802.1Q VLAN. At most one network may be untagged.

Read-Only:

- `connectivity` (String) public or private. Null when unknown.
- `fabric` (String) Fabric of the network. Null when unknown.
- `name` (String) Network name. Null when unknown.
- `vlan_id` (Number) VLAN ID. Null when unknown.

<a id="nestedatt--networks--ip_allocations"></a>
### Nested Schema for `networks.ip_allocations`

Optional:

- `family` (Number) 4 or 6.
- `prefix_id` (String) ID of a prefix in the network.

Read-Only:

- `address` (String) The address.
- `id` (String) IP allocation ID.
- `prefix` (Attributes) The prefix the address is in. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--networks--ip_allocations--prefix))

<a id="nestedatt--networks--ip_allocations--prefix"></a>
### Nested Schema for `networks.ip_allocations.prefix`

Read-Only:

- `cidr` (String) Prefix in CIDR notation.
- `gateway` (String) Gateway of the prefix. Null when it has none, for example on a private network.
- `id` (String) Prefix ID.




<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).


<a id="nestedatt--ip_addresses"></a>
### Nested Schema for `ip_addresses`

Read-Only:

- `ip_address` (String) Server IP address.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import i3dnet_flexmetal_server.my-server uuid
```
